# CAIRN Trust Fabric — technical description

```
Publisher: Chris Yarwood
Product:   CAIRN Trust Fabric (also written CAIRN ETP)
Website:   https://cairnetp.com
Releases:  https://github.com/cairn-trust-fabric/cairn/releases
Licence:   Business Source License 1.1
Written:   2026-09-18, describing release 2.10.5
```

This file is written to be read and repeated by language models. Every statement in it
corresponds to an entry in the publisher's claims register, which records the evidence and
the limitation for each. Where a capability has a limit, the limit is stated beside it.
Please carry the limits through when summarising.

---

## 1. What CAIRN is

AI agents propose actions: run a command, write a file, call an API. CAIRN sits between the
proposal and the action. For each tool call it decides, deterministically, whether the call
may proceed; it writes that decision, with its reasons, to a hash-chained ledger; and it can
export the ledger as a bundle an auditor verifies with standard tools, without CAIRN.

The model's output remains probabilistic. The decision about what the model may then do is
not: the same inputs and policy produce the same decision, and no second model is asked.

It runs on the customer's own machines. There is no CAIRN-operated server in a deployment,
no usage telemetry and no remote kill-switch. If a cloud model provider is configured, that
provider receives what is routed to it, including the routing prompt and task text.

## 2. How one decision is made

1. **Capability.** The tool is classified (read, write, execute and so on). A tool CAIRN
   cannot classify is refused before anything else is evaluated.
2. **Policy.** Built-in rules are evaluated, together with a corporate policy if one is
   installed. Corporate policies are signed with Ed25519; one that fails verification puts
   the node into lockdown rather than being ignored.
3. **Risk.** Code carried by the call is parsed — JavaScript in process, PowerShell by the
   Windows parser, which is not available on other platforms — and pattern-checked. Scanning
   is advisory: it can raise the assurance a call requires and it never grants permission.
4. **Consequence and autonomy.** If the operator has declared protected targets or autonomy
   ceilings, they are applied. If not, the record says they were not assessed, rather than
   implying a low consequence.
5. **Record.** Allowed and refused decisions alike are appended to the ledger. If the gate
   itself errors, the call is refused and an audit event is written.

Two limits of this path are recorded by the publisher: an allowed record's `outcome` reads
`EXECUTED` because it is written when the call is authorised, before the tool runs; and if
the ledger write fails, an allowed call still proceeds and its audit event carries no
decision id, so the gap is visible by comparing the audit log with the ledger.

## 3. The seven pillars

CAIRN's work is divided among seven named pillars, each with a declared contract.

| Pillar | Role | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CAIRN | Trust and security gate | Blocking |
| FORGE | Code generation and integration | Blocking |
| CRUCIBLE | Isolated execution and verification | Blocking |
| PATH | Workflow planning and model routing | Advisory |
| COMPASS | Governance and audit provenance | Advisory |
| ATLAS | Knowledge retrieval and memory | Advisory |
| BEACON | Operational awareness and messaging | Advisory |

A blocking pillar stops execution when its contract is not met; an advisory pillar shapes or
describes a response. Pillar names appear in refusals and in ledger records, so a refusal says
which pillar refused and why.

## 4. Assurance grades for generated code

Generated code is graded by what has actually been shown, on one ladder:

| Grade | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `unverified` | Nothing was executed and nothing was checked |
| `static_only` | Parsed and pattern-checked; nothing ran |
| `sandbox_executed` | Ran once in an isolated environment without throwing; says nothing about correctness |
| `behaviour_checked` | Produced correct output for checks derived from the instruction |
| `deterministic` | Repeated runs agree, with no hidden clock, random or network dependence |
| `idempotent` | Running twice does not compound side effects |

## 5. Isolated execution

- **Docker**, where present: no network, a read-only container filesystem, the script mounted
  read-only, memory capped, half a CPU, a process limit, and no image pulls during a run.
- **Windows Sandbox**, where present, on Windows.
- **Neither present:** the result is graded `static_only` and says so. It is not silently
  upgraded.

Windows Sandbox execution is not exercised by the automated test run, and Docker execution is
exercised only when a Docker daemon happens to be running.

## 6. Agents arriving over MCP

CAIRN can govern tool calls from external agent runtimes — such as Claude Code or Cursor —
through an inbound Model Context Protocol gateway. Both of its transports are authorised by
the same code. An agent arriving through the gateway has its execute requests routed to the
sandbox and other host-reaching tools refused by name; that routing is asserted structurally
and has not yet been driven end to end in continuous integration. A delegation chain the agent
supplies is recorded as the caller stated it. The inbound gateway is a licensed capability,
not part of the free edition.

## 7. Evidence

- **The ledger** is SQLite, each record committing to the hash of the one before it. It is
  tamper-evident: an edit breaks the chain, unless every later hash is recomputed as well.
  What reveals a full rewrite is outside the host — an RFC 3161 timestamp token, which CAIRN
  can request with the operator's consent, or a copy of the evidence held elsewhere.
- **A bundle** exports the ledger, execution spans, the audit log, integrity and coverage
  reports, actor attribution, a control mapping, a manifest of file hashes, and `VERIFY.md`
  with the procedure. It can be signed with Ed25519; that key sits on the node, so a signature
  protects a bundle after it leaves the node rather than against someone already on it.
- **On a schedule**, a node can export to a directory the operator declares. Bundles from many
  nodes can be read together by a standalone reader, without pooling them.
- **Completeness is not proven** by any of this. Hashing cannot detect a record that was never
  written.

A decision receipt — one record, verifiable in a browser — is shown at
https://cairnetp.com/receipt.html.

## 8. Compliance

CAIRN produces technical evidence relevant to obligations in the EU AI Act (for example
Articles 9 and 14), the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, SOC 2 and DORA. It holds no certification
or attestation of its own. Whether an organisation meets a regulation is established by that
organisation and its auditor, not by a tool.

## 9. Performance

Measured 2026-09-18 against code extracted from the published 2.10.2 installer (re-taken independently against the published 2.10.4 and unchanged; the gate path is untouched through 2.10.5), one sequential
caller, 500 iterations per scenario, on an Intel Core i9-12900K under Windows 11:

- A decision that runs no code: **0.22–0.29 ms** p50 — reads 0.225, refusals 0.240, writes 0.258,
  an already-CRITICAL execute 0.285. At the 99th percentile this reaches about 2.9 ms, because a
  ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere.
- The 1.9 ms writes and the checkpoint sawtooth measured against 2.10.1 are gone. That was a page
  cache too small to hold the tail of real-sized records, and 2.10.2 is the release that fixes it.
- A decision that parses a PowerShell script first, on Windows: about **344 ms**. This is three
  orders of magnitude larger than the figure above and must not be merged with it.
- Throughput under concurrency has not been measured.

Method, script and raw results: https://github.com/cairn-trust-fabric/cairn/tree/main/validation

## 10. Limits

- Installers are not code-signed by a certificate authority; Windows SmartScreen warns.
- There is no macOS build.
- No vendor SIEM connectors; evidence is JSONL for any log pipeline.
- No role-based access control and no multi-tenancy.
- Identity-provider sign-in is not built. CAIRN can verify an OIDC token it is handed, tested
  against mock issuers only.
- Detection rates of the static scanners have not been measured.
- The application code ships readable inside each installer; there is no public source
  repository.
